messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: occu function
parts:
Hi all,

I am using the unmarked package for a little while now and am very
happy with it, so thank you very much for all the effort you put into
that.

Now to my problem:

The model function I use is occu. So far I have used precreated model
sets like:

occu1<- occu(~1 ~near_frshwZ+UTM_E_UTM_N+FOR1_DA_100Z+FOR_1KZ, UMF)
occu2<- occu(~1 ~near_frshwZ+UTM_E_UTM_N+FOR1_DA_100Z+FOR_1KZ
+Lndar_1kmZ, UMF)
occu3<- occu(~1 ~near_frshwZ+UTM_E_UTM_N+FOR1_DA_100Z, UMF)

before doing

fitList()
and
modSel()

to rank the models used (before averaging them).

Right now I am trying to make a stepwise routine for model selection
using occu. The stepwise function I am editing is already working well
with functions from the lme4 package like lmer. I am running into some
very strange problems with occu though, which is the reason I am
posting here.

Now my null model is something like the following with a couple of
variables for both the detectability as well as the occupancy side:

BRCR<- occu(~ Lndar_1kmZ + FOR1_DA_1KZ + CR_CL_3Z + DATE_JUL + OCODES
~ rdl_up_100Z + FOR0_100Z + FOR1_DA_100Z + CR_CL0Z + CR_CL_3Z +
OF_100Z + DATE_JUL, UMF)

What the stepwise function is doing (or should do) is trying to remove
terms from the occupancy side. In this particular case it is producing
the following error though:

Error in parse(text = x) : unexpected symbol in:
"~Lndar_1kmZ + FOR1_DA_1KZ + CR_CL_3Z + DATE_JUL + OCODES ~near_saltwZ
+ Lndar_1kmZ + FOR_1KZ + SAV_1KMZ + SHR_1KMZ + RUR_100Z +
~Lndar_1kmZ + FOR1_DA_1KZ + CR_CL_3Z + DATE_JUL + OCODES
FOR1_DA_100Z"

For some strange reason the function tries to put the detectability
term into the occupancy term, in addition to the term it actually
should put in (FOR1_DA_100Z). The even stranger thing is that when I
remove one of the occupancy terms from the null model everything works
fine and there are no errors.

The part of the function where the error occurs is the following line
of code:

models[[j]] <- update(model.basis, as.formula(paste("~. ~. - ",
blocks[j])))

The thing I can think of that might produce a problem is with the two
'~' in the formula, where I am not sure if as.formula() will be able
to handle them correctly. Do any of you have any idea if this could
work or would it throw off the as.formula() function, resulting in the
strange error?

If this could be the issue would it help to change the occu function
call from occu(~p ~psi,UMF) to something like occu(~p, ~psi, UMF)?

If you have any other suggestions on the matter I would be very
grateful as this error is really puzzling me and being fairly new to R
I have not enough grasp on the subject efficiently find solutions for
this.

Thank you very much for you help,
Richard

messages.author: 9548b9e0c8258268
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] occu function
parts:
Hi Richard,

Glad you're happy with unmarked!

I think that you're right that the problem is most likely because of the double RH-sided formula that unmarked uses.  Any general code from another R package would need to be adapted to handle this and I would be surprised if any such code worked without careful adaptation!

That said, I don't have time to adapt it myself immediately, but it's on the to-do and anyone else is welcome to contribute such a thing!  I would suggest playing around with creating formulas as character strings through whatever means is necessary (likely with paste()), and then coercing to a formula with as.formula().  Another approach would be to write a small wrapper for occu() that had the desired input formula structure (2 formulas) and that calls unmarked's occu().  This might be easier to adapt the existing stepwise code.

I hope that helps,
Ian

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: occu function
parts:
Hi Richard,

Since your error occurs when calling update, you might want to look at
the method definition. This is an S4 method specific to unmarkedFit
objects, so you need to type the following to see the code:

getMethod(¨update¨, ¨unmarkedFit¨)

Richard

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: occu function
parts:
The bug has been fixed, and you can download the source from github:

http://github.com/ianfiske/unmarked

You can then unzip and build unmarked from source using:

R CMD build unmarked

R CMD INSTALL unmarked_0.8-3.tar.gz

If you use Windows, you will need Rtools
(http://www.murdoch-sutherland.com/Rtools/).

Note, that this is a development version and not as well tested.

Richard

Hi Hardin,

Thanks for the questions -- they're not too basic:

On Wed, Mar 17, 2010 at 1:49 PM, Hardin Waddle <wad...@usgs.gov> wrote:
I have two questions that I hope are not too basic with regards to the
colext() function, but they really apply to unmarked in general:

1.) I am testing unmarked and familiarizing myself with the package using
a simple simulated dataset.  I noticed that each time I run the analysis
on the same exact data I get a slightly different result for the estimates
and SEs.  This seems to be especially noticeable when parameters are
closest to their bounds (0 or 1), but it happens to all the parameters. Is
this normal?  I am using the default algorithm for optim ("BFGS"), but I
also tried "Nelder-Mead" and had the same result.  Is there some kind of
stochasticity involved here?

I just noticed that different fitting functions appear to handle missing starting values differently.  Some find random starts (e.g., colext()) and others always start at (0,0,..,0).  I justed added this to the to-do list (http://github.com/ianfiske/unmarked/issues/issue/26).  Regardless, do you see this behavior if you specify starting values with the starts argument?  It's probably just a consequence of random starting values.  And if the MLE is on the boundary, then the numerics will be more sensitive to starting values.

2.) Second, I would like to specify a model where p is different in
primary period 1 and primary period 2, but with no covariates.  And no
covariates on initial psi or gamma or epsilon.  Problem is I do not know
how to specify that using the syntax for unmarked.  Would someone mind
showing me how the formula for p= ~1 should be altered to allow a
different estimate of p for each primary period?

You need your unmarkedMultFrame to include an obsCovs variable for year.  So if you have M sites, T seasons, and J obs/season, then add this to your existing obsCovs with (warning, untested code follows)

obsCovs(umf) <- cbind(obsCovs(umf), year = as.factor(rep(rep(1:T, each = J), M))

Then specify pformula = ~ year and leave the other formulae as ~ 1.  That should do it if I get your question.

Thanks for your help,

Hardin
